# What Pulumi access tokens the library redacts, and what it leaves alone.
#
# Every token here is built from the ordered run 0123456789abcdef, which no real
# credential is: a body is forty hexadecimal characters, so the run twice over
# and eight more is one, and the prefix in front brings a token to forty-four.
# Where a case turns on the alphabet a body is written in, it carries the same
# run spelled uppercase or carried on past f instead.

patterns: pulumi-access-token

# The one prefix Pulumi writes a token with, in the places a token is written.
# There is a single kind of string here rather than a table of them: the token a
# user creates for themselves, the token an organization is issued and the token
# a team is issued share the prefix and carry no mark to tell one from another,
# so a caller enabling this pattern is enabling all three at once.

case:     a token in an environment assignment
in:       PULUMI_ACCESS_TOKEN=pul-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      PULUMI_ACCESS_TOKEN=«pulumi-access-token»

case:     a token in the header the rest api reads it from
in:       Authorization: token pul-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      Authorization: token «pulumi-access-token»

case:     a token in the credentials file the cli writes
in:       {"current":"https://api.pulumi.com","accessTokens":{"https://api.pulumi.com":"pul-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567"}}
out:      {"current":"https://api.pulumi.com","accessTokens":{"https://api.pulumi.com":"«pulumi-access-token»"}}

case:     a token in the yaml a deployment runner is configured with
in:       token: pul-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567\nversion: v0.0.5
out:      token: «pulumi-access-token»\nversion: v0.0.5

case:     a token in the json a token exchange returns
in:       {"accessToken":"pul-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567","tokenType":"Bearer","expiresIn":7200}
out:      {"accessToken":"«pulumi-access-token»","tokenType":"Bearer","expiresIn":7200}

case:     a token on a curl command line
in:       curl -H "Authorization: token pul-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567" https://api.pulumi.com/api/user
out:      curl -H "Authorization: token «pulumi-access-token»" https://api.pulumi.com/api/user

# The alphabet the forty characters are written in: lowercase hexadecimal, which
# is what two of the three rules reading this format ask for. The third reads the
# same count through a class holding every lowercase letter, and that class is
# the widening the pattern's own file declines. A body carrying anything outside
# hexadecimal is no body at all.

case:     an uppercase body
in:       pul-0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF01234567
out:      pul-0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF01234567

case:     one uppercase character in a body
in:       pul-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456F
out:      pul-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456F

case:     a body carrying letters past f
in:       pul-0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123
out:      pul-0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123

case:     a body carrying an underscore
in:       pul-0123456789abcdef_123456789abcdef01234567
out:      pul-0123456789abcdef_123456789abcdef01234567

case:     a body carrying a hyphen
in:       pul-0123456789abcdef-123456789abcdef01234567
out:      pul-0123456789abcdef-123456789abcdef01234567

# The lengths either side of forty. That count is what every published rule
# reading this format asks for, and it is used as a count rather than a floor:
# thirty-nine characters are not a token, and forty-one are a token and one
# character that belongs to no credential. The second of those is the price of
# having no boundary behind the match — a boundary there would drop this token
# rather than trim it, and a real token written against a digit would come
# through whole.

case:     a body of forty characters is a token
in:       pul-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      «pulumi-access-token»

case:     a body of thirty-nine characters is not
in:       pul-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456
out:      pul-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456

case:     an alphabet run longer than a token is a token and what follows it
in:       pul-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef012345678
out:      «pulumi-access-token»8

# What a token may be written against. The prefix is the whole of the anchor and
# there is no boundary on either side of it, so a token keeps its span whatever
# word character it abuts.

case:     a token after an underscore
in:       PULUMI_ACCESS_TOKEN_pul-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      PULUMI_ACCESS_TOKEN_«pulumi-access-token»

case:     a token after a letter
in:       xpul-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      x«pulumi-access-token»

case:     a word written against a token
in:       pul-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567suffix
out:      «pulumi-access-token»suffix

case:     a token at the end of a sentence
in:       the token is pul-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567.
out:      the token is «pulumi-access-token».

# Two tokens written together. No token can begin inside another here: everything
# a span covers past the prefix is hexadecimal, and the p the prefix opens with
# is neither of the letters behind it, is not the hyphen closing it and is no
# character a body may hold. So two tokens written with nothing between them are
# two separate values and both go, and a prefix standing where a body would have
# to hold it ends the candidate in front of it and opens the token itself.

case:     two tokens with nothing between them
in:       pul-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567pul-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      «pulumi-access-token»«pulumi-access-token»

case:     a prefix written in front of a token
in:       pul-pul-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      pul-«pulumi-access-token»

# What this pattern redacts that nobody issued. Forty lowercase hexadecimal
# characters behind the prefix is the format every rule reading it asks for, and
# a SHA-1 is forty of them, so the prefix written straight in front of one is a
# token character for character and the whole of it goes. A SHA-256 is longer and
# is redacted for forty-four characters with the rest left in the text — which is
# reachable, because the rules reading this format ask that no word character
# stand in front of a match and this pattern does not: the name of a
# content-addressed asset is a word, a hyphen and a digest, and where that word
# ends in the letters the prefix opens with the digest behind it is read as a
# body. That is the answer rather than a fault in it. Sparing these would mean
# asking what stands in front of a token, and a token written against an
# underscore is how one reaches a log line from a shell; what is taken instead is
# a stretch of a value that was already opaque.

case:     the prefix in front of a sha-1
in:       pul-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      «pulumi-access-token»

case:     the prefix in front of a sha-256
in:       pul-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      «pulumi-access-token»89abcdef0123456789abcdef

case:     a word ending in the letters of the prefix in front of a digest
in:       assets/vipul-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef.png
out:      assets/vi«pulumi-access-token»89abcdef0123456789abcdef.png

# And what this pattern leaves alone. The first three are the prefix, which is
# read in the case Pulumi writes it and with every character of it. Then the
# digest the count turns away, a run of the right length with no prefix in front
# of it, and a UUID, whose hyphens are no character a body may hold. The last two
# carry no prefix at all: a hexadecimal run holds none of the four characters a
# prefix is written with, so no digest carries one partway along.

case:     an uppercase prefix
in:       PUL-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      PUL-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567

case:     the prefix without the hyphen closing it
in:       pul0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef012345678
out:      pul0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef012345678

case:     an underscore where the prefix closes
in:       pul_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      pul_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567

case:     the prefix in front of an md5
in:       pul-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      pul-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef

case:     a run of the right length opening with no prefix
in:       xxxx0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      xxxx0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567

case:     a uuid behind the prefix
in:       pul-01234567-89ab-cdef-0123-456789abcdef
out:      pul-01234567-89ab-cdef-0123-456789abcdef

case:     a digest with no prefix
in:       sha=0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      sha=0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567

case:     prose
in:       there is no credential in this sentence
out:      there is no credential in this sentence

# And the text a token is written among, which this pattern has nothing to say
# about. The word Pulumi's own host name and its CLI are spelled with opens with
# the three letters of the prefix, and the hyphen closing that prefix is what
# turns each of them away.

case:     a log line naming the api a token authenticates against
in:       time=2026-08-17T00:00:00Z level=info msg="updating stack" url=https://api.pulumi.com/api/user/stacks
out:      time=2026-08-17T00:00:00Z level=info msg="updating stack" url=https://api.pulumi.com/api/user/stacks

case:     the command line a stack is updated from
in:       pulumi up --yes --stack acme/website/prod --non-interactive
out:      pulumi up --yes --stack acme/website/prod --non-interactive

case:     the backend a token authenticates against
in:       PULUMI_BACKEND_URL=https://api.pulumi.com
out:      PULUMI_BACKEND_URL=https://api.pulumi.com
